stories.title: Petition would criminalize filming/posting people in crisis — sponsored by Liberal MP Arielle Kayabaga
stories.angle: Big Canadian free-speech vs dignity fight for THE LIST: Commons e-petition e-7621, sponsored by Deputy Government House Leader Arielle Kayabaga, asks for a Criminal Code offence for knowingly recording someone in a 'prescribed circumstance of significant vulnerability' — homelessness, mental-health crisis, substance impairment — for the purpose of publishing it. Blacklock frames it as a bid to ban posting photos of homeless people or street addicts online. You're asking listeners: protect dignity, or criminalize ugly street reality?

Would create Criminal Code offence for knowingly recording a vulnerable person in public to publish/distribute
Prescribed vulnerability includes homelessness, mental-health crisis, significant substance impairment
Blacklock: follows complaints about needles/disorder — critics will call it a street-photo ban
Caller fuel: dignity and safety for people in crisis vs. chilling citizen journalism / accountability
stories.debate: Should Canada criminalize filming and posting people in visible crisis — or is that how we stop seeing the problem?
